15. Interview Revision — Week 33

Q1. What are the three ways to author an AWS Glue job?

Answer: Visual ETL, Interactive Notebooks, and Script Editor.

Q2. What is the difference between G.1X and G.2X?

Answer: G.1X provides 4 vCPUs and 16 GB RAM, while G.2X provides 8 vCPUs and 32 GB RAM per worker.

Q3. What does Change Schema do?

Answer: It can rename columns, change data types, and remove unwanted fields.

Q4. Why is Glue Data Catalog important?

Answer: It stores metadata describing datasets, schemas, partitions, and table structures used by Glue and other AWS analytics services.

Q5. What is the purpose of a Glue Crawler?

Answer: It discovers data structures, infers schemas, detects partitions, and registers metadata in the Glue Data Catalog.

Q6. What are the three PII global actions?

Answer:

DETECT

REDACT

SHA256_HASH

Q7. What is the difference between row-level and column-level sensitive-data detection?

Answer: Row-level detection scans individual cells/rows to identify specific PII instances, whereas column-level detection determines whether an entire column should be treated as sensitive based on sampled detection and a threshold.

Q8. What is DQDL?

Answer: Data Quality Definition Language, used to define AWS Glue Data Quality rules.

Q9. What framework powers Glue Data Quality?

Answer: The course identifies the open-source DeeQu framework.

Q10. Why convert DynamicFrames to DataFrames?

Answer: To use standard PySpark DataFrame APIs and functions when implementing custom transformation logic.

Q11. Why does a custom transform return a DynamicFrameCollection?

Answer: It allows a custom transformation to produce one or multiple DynamicFrames as outputs.

Q12. Why use Select From Collection?

Answer: To extract a specific DynamicFrame from the returned DynamicFrameCollection for downstream processing.

Q13. How do you make a custom transformation reusable?

Answer: Package the transformation configuration and implementation into the required JSON and Python files and place them in the Glue assets transforms/ location so they can be exposed as reusable visual nodes.

Week 34: AWS Object Storage, Event-Driven Compute & Redshift Enterprise Data Warehousing

1. Amazon S3 — Object Storage & Lifecycle Management

Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is AWS object storage designed for storing and retrieving virtually unlimited amounts of unstructured and semi-structured data.

S3 Object Hierarchy

GLOBAL AWS NAMESPACE

        │

        ▼

     REGION

   (us-east-1)

        │

        ▼

     BUCKET

   (tt-s3-demo-1)

        │

        ▼

    OBJECT KEY

 (input/orders.csv)

        │

        ├── Object Data / Payload

        └── Metadata + Access Policies

Key S3 Concepts

Concept

Meaning

Object Storage

Data is stored as objects identified by keys

Bucket

Logical container for objects

Object Key

Complete identifier/path of an object

Region

AWS geographical location hosting the bucket

Object Payload

Actual stored data

Metadata

Information associated with the object

Important Limits / Characteristics

  • Designed durability: 99.999999999% (11 9s)
  • A single object can be up to 5 TB
  • Bucket names have a global namespace
  • S3 is fundamentally object storage, not a traditional hierarchical filesystem.

2. S3 Storage Classes

S3 provides multiple storage classes based on access frequency, retrieval requirements, and cost.

Storage Class

Access Pattern

Typical Usage

S3 Standard

Frequent

Active data lakes and frequently accessed data

S3 Intelligent-Tiering

Unknown/changing

Automatically optimizes storage cost

S3 Standard-IA

Infrequent

Backups and DR data

S3 Express One Zone

High-performance, low latency

Latency-sensitive workloads

S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

Rare but immediate

Compliance/archive data needing fast retrieval

S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

Rare

Historical archives

S3 Glacier Deep Archive

Extremely rare

Long-term preservation

Lifecycle Management

Instead of manually moving files between storage tiers, S3 Lifecycle Rules can automate transitions.

         DATA AGE

             │

             ▼

      S3 STANDARD

      Active / Hot

             │

          30 Days

             ▼

      S3 STANDARD-IA

      Infrequent Data

             │

         365 Days

             ▼

   S3 GLACIER DEEP ARCHIVE

      Long-Term Data

Core Idea

Store hot data in expensive/high-performance tiers and automatically transition older data to cheaper archival tiers.

This reduces long-term storage cost without requiring manual movement of objects.

3. AWS Lambda — Event-Driven Serverless Compute

AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that executes code in response to events.

Examples:

  • S3 object upload
  • API Gateway request
  • Other AWS service events

The key advantage is that you don't provision or manage servers.

S3 → Lambda Architecture

            SOURCE S3 BUCKET

                   │

            Upload logs.csv

                   │

                   ▼

          ObjectCreated Event

                   │

                   ▼

             AWS LAMBDA

          lambda_handler()

                   │

          boto3 copy_object()

                   │

                   ▼

          TARGET S3 BUCKET

Lambda Execution Characteristics

  • Maximum execution time: 15 minutes / 900 seconds
  • Automatically scales horizontally with incoming requests.
  • Suitable for event-driven, short-lived workloads.
  • Not intended for long-running processing jobs.

4. Lambda S3 Event Handler

The Lambda function receives information about the newly created S3 object through the event payload.

Event Information

event

 └── Records[]

      └── s3

           ├── bucket

           │    └── name

           └── object

                └── key

The application extracts:

source_bucket = event['Records'][0]['s3']['bucket']['name']

source_key = event['Records'][0]['s3']['object']['key']

A destination bucket can be retrieved from an environment variable:

destination_bucket = os.environ.get("target_bucket")

Then the object can be copied using the AWS SDK:

s3_client.copy_object(

    Bucket=destination_bucket,

    CopySource={'Bucket': source_bucket, 'Key': source_key},

    Key=destination_key

)

Production Design Principle

The S3 client is initialized outside the Lambda handler:

s3_client = boto3.client('s3')

This allows the execution environment to potentially reuse the client across invocations.

5. Lambda Layers

A Lambda Layer is a reusable .zip package containing dependencies or shared code that can be attached to Lambda functions.

Useful for:

  • Custom Python modules
  • pandas
  • requests
  • Other reusable libraries

Layer Structure

lambda_layer.zip

└── python/

    └── lib/

        └── python3.12/

            └── site-packages/

                └── custom_module/

Why Use Layers?

Without layers:

Lambda Function A ──> pandas

Lambda Function B ──> pandas

Lambda Function C ──> pandas

With a shared layer:

                ┌── Lambda A

                 │

Shared Layer ────┼── Lambda B

                 │

                 └── Lambda C

Key benefit: reusable dependencies can be maintained independently from individual Lambda deployment packages.

6. Amazon Redshift — Enterprise Data Warehouse

Amazon Redshift is a managed, cloud-based OLAP data warehouse designed for large-scale analytical workloads.

Its architecture is based on Massively Parallel Processing (MPP).

                    CLIENT APPLICATIONS

                  BI Tools / SQL / ETL

                           │

                           ▼

                    ┌─────────────┐

                    │ LEADER NODE │

                    ├─────────────┤

                    │ Parse SQL   │

                    │ Optimize    │

                    │ Plan Query  │

                    └──────┬──────┘

                           │

             ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐

             ▼                           ▼

      COMPUTE NODE 1              COMPUTE NODE 2

      ┌─────────────┐             ┌─────────────┐

      │ Slice 0     │             │ Slice 0     │

      │ Slice 1     │             │ Slice 1     │

      └─────────────┘             └─────────────┘

Redshift Components

1. Leader Node

Responsible for:

  • Receiving client queries
  • Parsing SQL
  • Creating optimized execution plans
  • Compiling query code
  • Distributing work
  • Aggregating results

2. Compute Nodes

Execute the actual query-processing workload against distributed data.

3. Slices

Each compute node is divided into virtual slices.

Each slice manages a portion of:

  • CPU
  • Memory
  • Disk

This enables parallel execution.

7. Redshift Performance Optimization

Redshift's analytical performance comes from several architectural features.

Columnar Storage

Instead of storing:

Row 1 → A B C D

Row 2 → A B C D

Row 3 → A B C D

Redshift stores values by column:

Column A → A A A

Column B → B B B

Column C → C C C

Column D → D D D

If a query needs only two columns, unnecessary data does not need to be read.

MPP

Large queries are distributed across multiple compute slices.

Column Compression

Compression reduces:

  • Storage footprint
  • Disk I/O
  • Amount of data processed

Result Set Caching

Previously generated query results can be cached, allowing identical subsequent queries to return much faster.

8. Redshift Distribution Styles

Distribution determines where rows are physically stored across compute-node slices.

               DISTRIBUTION STYLES

        EVEN          KEY             ALL

          │             │              │

          ▼             ▼              ▼

     Round Robin    Hash Key      Full Copy

          │             │              │

          ▼             ▼              ▼

     Balanced       Same Keys      Every Node

     Distribution   Same Slice

Distribution Style Comparison

Style

Mechanism

Best Use

AUTO

Redshift chooses distribution strategy

Default/general workloads

EVEN

Round-robin distribution

Tables without strong join relationships

KEY

Hashes a selected column

Frequently joined large tables

ALL

Copies table to every node

Small dimension tables

KEY Distribution

Suppose:

DISTKEY = customer_id

Rows with the same customer ID are directed to the same slice.

This can reduce network data movement during joins.

9. Redshift Sort Keys

A SORTKEY determines the physical ordering of data within storage blocks.

Zone Map Pruning

Redshift maintains metadata about values contained in blocks.

For example:

Block 1 → order_id: 1–1000

Block 2 → order_id: 1001–2000

Block 3 → order_id: 2001–3000

If the query asks:

WHERE order_id = 2500

Redshift can skip Blocks 1 and 2 and scan only Block 3.

Sort Merge Bucket (SMB) Joins

Using compatible distribution and sorting strategies can allow highly efficient local merge joins without unnecessary:

  • Network shuffling
  • Sorting

10. DISTKEY + SORTKEY Example

CREATE TABLE retail_db.public.orders (

    order_id INTEGER,

    order_date VARCHAR(100),

    order_customer_id INTEGER DISTKEY,

    order_status VARCHAR(30)

)

SORTKEY(order_id);

Here:

order_customer_id → DISTKEY

order_id          → SORTKEY

Remember

DISTKEY controls WHERE data goes.

SORTKEY controls HOW data is physically ordered.

This distinction is extremely important in Redshift interviews.

11. Redshift Spectrum — Query S3 Without Loading Data

Redshift Spectrum allows Redshift to query data directly in Amazon S3.

                   REDSHIFT

                Leader + Compute

                      │

             ┌────────┴────────┐

             │                 │

             ▼                 ▼

      Local Redshift      Redshift Spectrum

         Tables                 │

                                ▼

                       AWS Glue Catalog

                                │

                                ▼

                            Amazon S3

                     CSV / Parquet / ORC

Why Spectrum?

Traditional approach:

S3 → COPY → Redshift → Query

Spectrum:

S3 ───────────────────────→ Query directly

             ↑

        Redshift Spectrum

This is particularly useful when data is too large or unnecessary to fully ingest into Redshift.

12. Spectrum External Schema

An external schema connects Redshift to the AWS Glue Data Catalog.

CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA spectrum

FROM DATA CATALOG

DATABASE 'retaildemo'

IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftSpectrumRole'

CREATE EXTERNAL DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS;

Then an external table can point to S3:

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE spectrum.orders (

    order_id INTEGER,

    order_date VARCHAR(100),

    order_customer_id INTEGER,

    order_status VARCHAR(30)

)

ROW FORMAT DELIMITED FIELDS TERMINATED BY ','

STORED AS TEXTFILE

LOCATION 's3://tt-redshift-demo/retail-data/orders';

The table definition is in the catalog, while the actual data remains in S3.

13. Federated Query — S3 + Redshift

One powerful use case is joining:

  • External S3 data
  • Internal Redshift tables

SELECT

    o.order_id,

    o.order_date,

    c.customer_fname,

    c.customer_lname

FROM spectrum.orders o

JOIN retail_db.public.customers c

  ON o.order_customer_id = c.customer_id;

Conceptually:

S3 Orders

    │

    │ Spectrum

    ▼

External Table

    │

    ├──────── JOIN ────────┐

    │                      │

    ▼                      ▼

Redshift Customers    Query Result

14. Redshift COPY Command

The COPY command is designed for high-throughput bulk loading of data from S3 into Redshift.

COPY retail_db.sales.orders

FROM 's3://tt-redshift-demo/retail-data/orders/'

IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftAccessRole'

FORMAT AS CSV

DELIMITER ','

IGNOREHEADER 1

REGION AS 'us-east-1';

Basic Flow

S3 Files

   │

   ▼

COPY Command

   │

   ▼

Parallel Loading

   │

   ▼

Redshift Managed Storage

COPY vs Spectrum

Feature

COPY

Spectrum

Data location

Moves into Redshift

Remains in S3

Primary purpose

Data ingestion

Query external data

Processing

Redshift-managed storage

S3 + Spectrum

Week 35: Enterprise AWS Incremental Data Engineering Pipeline

Week 35 focuses on building a resilient, event-driven, production-grade incremental ETL pipeline on AWS. This architecture handles incremental extraction from relational stores (AWS RDS MySQL), landing raw data into Amazon S3, triggering serverless validation workflows (AWS Lambda + Glue), and staging optimized data into Amazon Redshift for enterprise analytics.

               [ Production AWS Incremental Pipeline Architecture ]

   +----------------+     Glue Incremental Extract     +-----------------------+

   |  AWS RDS MySQL | -------------------------------> | S3 Raw Landing Bucket |

   | (Relational)   |    (Watermarking State Query)    | (Compressed Parquet)  |

   +----------------+                                  +-----------------------+

                                                                   |

                                                         S3 Event Notification

                                                                   v

   +--------------------+    Trigger Execution     +-----------------------+

   | AWS Glue ETL Job   | <----------------------- |  AWS Lambda Function  |

   | (DQDL & Masking)   |                          |  (Event Dispatcher)   |

   +--------------------+                          +-----------------------+

             |

             v

   +-----------------------+       Redshift Spectrum       +-----------------------+

   | S3 Staging Bucket     | <--------------------------- | Amazon Redshift DWH   |

   | (Parquet + Partitions)|    (External Glue Schema)    | (Data Warehouse)      |

   +-----------------------+                              +-----------------------+

1. Incremental Extraction & Watermarking Pattern

To avoid expensive full-table scans, an incremental extraction pattern isolates only newly inserted or modified records based on a tracking column (updated_at or last_modified timestamp).

Watermark Tracking Strategy

  1. State Store: A dedicated table (watermark_tracker) in RDS or DynamoDB tracks the latest execution timestamp for each source table.
  2. Extraction Query: The extraction job selects records where updated_at > MAX(last_success_timestamp).
  3. Commit Phase: Once S3 writes complete successfully, the state store is updated with the max timestamp from the extracted batch.

Unabridged Glue Extraction Job (glue_incremental_extract.py)

import sys

from awsglue.utils import getResolvedOptions

from pyspark.context import SparkContext

from awsglue.context import GlueContext

from awsglue.job import Job

from awsglue import DynamicFrame

from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Initialize AWS Glue and Spark Contexts

args = getResolvedOptions(sys.argv, ['JOB_NAME'])

sc = SparkContext()

glueContext = GlueContext(sc)

spark = glueContext.spark_session

job = Job(glueContext)

job.init(args['JOB_NAME'], args)

# 1. Read source data and watermark tracking state table from AWS RDS MySQL

orders_dyf = glueContext.create_dynamic_frame.from_options(

    connection_type="mysql",

    connection_options={"useConnectionProperties": "true", "dbtable": "orders", "connectionName": "RDS_MySQL_Conn"}

)

watermark_dyf = glueContext.create_dynamic_frame.from_options(

    connection_type="mysql",

    connection_options={"useConnectionProperties": "true", "dbtable": "watermark_tracker", "connectionName": "RDS_MySQL_Conn"}

)

orders_dyf.toDF().createOrReplaceTempView("src_orders")

watermark_dyf.toDF().createOrReplaceTempView("src_watermark")

# 2. Extract only incremental records modified since the last watermark execution

incremental_df = spark.sql("""

    SELECT * FROM src_orders

    WHERE updated_at > (

        SELECT COALESCE(MAX(last_success_timestamp), '1900-01-01 00:00:00')

        FROM src_watermark WHERE table_name = 'orders'

    )

""")

# 3. Save extracted incremental batch to S3 Landing Zone in compressed Parquet format

if incremental_df.count() > 0:

    output_dyf = DynamicFrame.fromDF(incremental_df.coalesce(1), glueContext, "output_dyf")

   

    glueContext.write_dynamic_frame.from_options(

        frame=output_dyf,

        connection_type="s3",

        connection_options={"path": "s3://production-data-lake-raw/landing/orders/"},

        format="glueparquet",

        format_options={"compression": "snappy"}

    )

   

    # 4. Update the Watermark State Table with the new maximum batch timestamp

    new_max_ts = incremental_df.agg(F.max("updated_at")).collect()[0][0]

    update_watermark_df = spark.createDataFrame([(new_max_ts, 'orders')], ['last_success_timestamp', 'table_name'])

   

    glueContext.write_dynamic_frame.from_options(

        frame=DynamicFrame.fromDF(update_watermark_df, glueContext, "update_watermark_df"),

        connection_type="mysql",

        connection_options={"useConnectionProperties": "true", "dbtable": "watermark_tracker", "connectionName": "RDS_MySQL_Conn"}

    )

job.commit()

2. Event-Driven Lambda Dispatcher Strategy

When new files hit the S3 Landing Zone, an S3 ObjectCreated event triggers a serverless AWS Lambda Function. The function parses the event payload and starts the downstream AWS Glue ETL processing job.

import boto3

import os

glue_client = boto3.client('glue')

def lambda_handler(event, context):

    # Parse event metadata from S3 trigger notification

    source_bucket = event['Records'][0]['s3']['bucket']['name']

    source_key = event['Records'][0]['s3']['object']['key']

   

    target_job_name = os.environ.get("GLUE_JOB_NAME", "pyspark_data_cleansing_job")

   

    # Pass input file details directly to Glue Job arguments

    response = glue_client.start_job_run(

        JobName=target_job_name,

        Arguments={

            '--SOURCE_BUCKET': source_bucket,

            '--SOURCE_KEY': source_key

        }

    )

   

    return {

        'statusCode': 200,

        'body': f"Triggered Glue Job {target_job_name} with RunId {response['JobRunId']}"

    }

4. Querying S3 Staging Data via Amazon Redshift Spectrum

Once transformed data lands in the S3 Processed Zone, Amazon Redshift Spectrum enables querying Parquet files directly using standard Redshift SQL queries without loading data onto Redshift disks.

-- 1. Create External Schema pointing to Glue Data Catalog Database

CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA spectrum_sales_schema

FROM DATA CATALOG DATABASE 'analytics_catalog_db'

IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedshiftSpectrumRole'

CREATE EXTERNAL DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS;

-- 2. Define External Table matching Parquet structure in S3 Staging Bucket

CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE spectrum_sales_schema.ext_orders (

    order_id BIGINT,

    customer_id BIGINT,

    amount DOUBLE PRECISION,

    order_status VARCHAR(50)

)

PARTITIONED BY (order_date VARCHAR(10))

STORED AS PARQUET

LOCATION 's3://production-data-lake-processed/orders/';

-- 3. Synchronize Partitions

ALTER TABLE spectrum_sales_schema.ext_orders RECOVER PARTITIONS;

-- 4. Execute Federated Query joining Redshift internal tables with S3 external tables

SELECT

    c.customer_name,

    COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders,

    SUM(o.amount) AS total_spend

FROM public.dim_customers c

JOIN spectrum_sales_schema.ext_orders o

  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id

WHERE o.order_date = '2026-07-25'

GROUP BY c.customer_name;

5. Technical Interview Q&A — AWS Incremental Pipelines

Q1: How do you handle schema evolution when performing incremental loads from S3 into Amazon Redshift?

Answer: Schema changes (like adding new columns) can break static copy jobs.

  1. AWS Glue Data Catalog Integration: AWS Glue Crawlers automatically detect new columns in Parquet files and update table definitions in the Glue Data Catalog.
  2. Redshift Spectrum: Spectrum dynamically queries updated Parquet schemas using the Glue Data Catalog, returning NULL values for older Parquet files that lack newly added columns.
  3. Redshift COPY Command: When loading directly into internal Redshift tables, use the FORMAT AS PARQUET option along with explicit column mapping to align file attributes with database definitions.

Q2: What is the difference between AWS Lambda event triggers and Amazon EventBridge rules for pipeline orchestration?

Answer:

  • AWS Lambda S3 Event Triggers: Best for direct 1-to-1 event notifications (e.g., executing a single function immediately when a specific S3 file arrives).
  • Amazon EventBridge: An enterprise event bus used for complex routing, event filtering, batching, and multi-target fan-out workflows (e.g., routing S3 object events to multiple target services like Glue, SQS, SNS, and Step Functions simultaneously).

2. Fundamental Array Algorithms & Coding Implementations

2.1 Two-Sum Problem (LeetCode #1)

Find indices of two numbers in an array nums that add up to a specified target.

Approaches:

  • Brute-Force — O(n²) Time, O(1) Space: Uses two nested loops to test every combination.
  • Sorting & Two-Pointers — O(n log n) Time, O(n) Space: Sorts an array copy and adjusts left/right pointers based on sum.
  • Hash Map Lookup — O(n) Time, O(n) Space: Computes complement = target - num and checks dictionary membership in a single pass.

from typing import List

class Solution:

    def twoSum(self, nums: List[int], target: int) -> List[int]:

        seen = {}  # Map value to index

        for i, num in enumerate(nums):

            complement = target - num

            if complement in seen:

                return [seen[complement], i]

            seen[num] = i

        return []

2.2 Single Number (LeetCode #136) — Bitwise XOR Optimization

Find the single element in an array where every other element appears twice.

Using the properties of Bitwise XOR (⊕):

  • x ⊕ x = 0
  • x ⊕ 0 = x

Duplicate numbers evaluate to zero, leaving only the unique value.

class Solution:

    def singleNumber(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:

        result = 0

        for num in nums:

            result ^= num  # XOR bitwise operation

        return result

Time Complexity: O(n)
Space Complexity: O(1)

2.3 Majority Element (LeetCode #169) — Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm

Find the element appearing more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times.

class Solution:

    def majorityElement(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:

        candidate = None

        count = 0

        for num in nums:

            if count == 0:

                candidate = num

            count += (1 if num == candidate else -1)

        return candidate

Time Complexity: O(n)
Space Complexity: O(1)

2.4 Maximum Subarray (LeetCode #53) — Kadane's Algorithm

Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum. Resets the running current sum to zero whenever it drops below zero.

class Solution:

    def maxSubArray(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:

        max_sum = nums[0]

        current_sum = 0

        for num in nums:

            if current_sum < 0:

                current_sum = 0

            current_sum += num

            if current_sum > max_sum:

                max_sum = current_sum

        return max_sum

Time Complexity: O(n)
Space Complexity: O(1)

2.5 Array Rotation in Place (LeetCode #189)

Rotate an array to the right by k steps using three array reversals.

class Solution:

    def reverse(self, nums: List[int], start: int, end: int) -> None:

        while start < end:

            nums[start], nums[end] = nums[end], nums[start]

            start += 1

            end -= 1

    def rotate(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> None:

        n = len(nums)

        k %= n

        self.reverse(nums, 0, n - 1)  # Reverse entire array

        self.reverse(nums, 0, k - 1)  # Reverse first k elements

        self.reverse(nums, k, n - 1)  # Reverse remaining elements

3. Linked List Algorithms & Fast/Slow Pointer Mechanics

                   [ Fast & Slow Pointer Traversal ]

   head ──> [ 1 ] ──> [ 2 ] ──> [ 3 ] ──> [ 4 ] ──> [ 5 ] ──> NULL

             ▲                  ▲

             │                  │

           Slow (1 step)      Fast (2 steps)

3.1 Reverse a Singly Linked List — Iterative Three-Pointer Approach

Reverses pointers in place using prev, curr, and temp_next pointers.

class ListNode:

    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):

        self.val = val

        self.next = next

class Solution:

    def reverseList(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:

        prev = None

        curr = head

        while curr is not None:

            temp_next = curr.next

            curr.next = prev

            prev = curr

            curr = temp_next

        return prev

Time Complexity: O(n)
Space Complexity: O(1)

3.2 Find Middle of Linked List — Floyd's Fast & Slow Pointers

The fast pointer moves two steps while the slow pointer moves one step. When the fast pointer reaches the end, the slow pointer rests at the exact middle node.

class Solution:

    def middleNode(self, head: ListNode) -> ListNode:

        slow = head

        fast = head

        while fast is not None and fast.next is not None:

            slow = slow.next

            fast = fast.next.next

        return slow

4. Specialized Data Engineering Structure: Bloom Filters

A Bloom Filter is a space-efficient, probabilistic data structure designed to quickly verify whether an element is guaranteed not in a set or possibly in a set.

Example use case: checking whether a user ID or email exists in disk storage before executing expensive I/O operations.

                    [ Bloom Filter Membership Verification ]

  Input Key ("trendytech.sumit@gmail.com")

        │

        ├── Hash Function 1 ──> Bit Array Index 2

        ├── Hash Function 2 ──> Bit Array Index 5

        └── Hash Function 3 ──> Bit Array Index 9

                                    │

                                    v

     Bit Array:  [0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0]

                          ▲           ▲               ▲

Bloom Filter Properties

  • False Positives ARE Possible: Multiple keys can set the same bit positions, causing the system to indicate an item exists when it does not.
  • False Negatives ARE IMPOSSIBLE: If any hash bit index returns 0, the element is guaranteed to not exist in the underlying dataset.

Week 37: Interview Preparation, ATS Resume Engineering & Job Search Strategy

1. ATS-Compliant Resume Architecture & Formatting Rules

An Applicant Tracking System (ATS) parses resume text into standardized database categories prior to recruiter review.

                    [ High-Impact ATS Resume Structure ]

  =============================================================================

  FULL NAME | AWS/Azure Certified Senior Data Engineer

  Phone Number | Professional Email | LinkedIn URL | Portfolio/GitHub

  =============================================================================

  PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

  4-5 lines summarizing years of experience, core cloud stack, and business impact.

  =============================================================================

  TECHNICAL SKILLS

  Cloud Platforms, Big Data Frameworks, Databases, Languages, Orchestration

  =============================================================================

  PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

  Reverse Chronological: Action Verb + Task / Scope + Quantified Result

  =============================================================================

  PROJECT HIGHLIGHTS

  Problem Statement ──> Architecture / Pipeline ──> Business Metric

  =============================================================================

  EDUCATION & CERTIFICATIONS

  Degree, College/University, Graduation Year | Official Cloud Certifications

  =============================================================================

Core Resume Writing Standards

1. Length Threshold

  • Maximum 1 page for professionals with under 2 years of experience.
  • Maximum 2 pages for experienced candidates.

2. Bullet Construction Formula

Bullet Formula:

Action Verb + Technical Scope/Task + Quantified Impact Metric

Weak Example:

Worked on building Data Pipelines in Azure Data Factory.

Strong Example:

Engineered 12+ automated Azure Data Factory ETL pipelines, ingesting 500 GB daily data into Delta Lake and reducing data turnaround time by 35%.

3. Action Verb Upgrades

Replace passive phrases such as:

  • Involved in
  • Worked on
  • Responsible for

With high-impact active verbs:

  • Pioneered
  • Engineered
  • Optimized
  • Architected
  • Automated
  • Streamlined

2. Naukri.com Platform Profile Optimization

To maximize visibility in recruiter queries, configure your Naukri profile to align with search algorithms.

                 [ Naukri Recruiter Visibility Strategy ]

      Profile Creation (100% Completion)

                         │

Naukri Key Configuration Settings

Resume Headline

The resume headline should highlight:

  • Designation
  • Total experience
  • Primary technology stack
  • Key achievements
  • Certifications

Template:

Skilled [Designation] with [X] Years experience specializing in [Key Skills] | [Education] from [Institute] with [Certification Name].

Example:

Skilled Data Engineer with 4 Years experience in PySpark, Databricks & Azure Data Factory | Built pipelines processing 100+ TB data | B.Tech NIT with AWS Certified Developer Associate.

Algorithm Refresh Trigger

Re-uploading your resume document every 14–15 days updates your "Last Active" timestamp, placing your profile at the top of recruiter searches.

Notice Period & Salary Range

Setting notice periods to under 30 days can increase recruiter call rates. Set realistic preferred salary expectations based on market averages.

LinkedIn enables both inbound recruiter reach-outs and targeted job applications.

  • Your fit for the role
